payload.title: Dual-write: every Item writer keeps headStageKey on the head row only
payload.description: One helper (content_item_lifecycle.head_stage_fields) returns {headStageKey: stage} for the row being made head and {headStageKey: None} for the row being superseded; every writer that sets stage or versionState uses it in the write it already makes: publishing.save_item (create), publishing.publish_item (head and the sibling supersede loop), publishing.unpublish_item, story_reporting.save_story_version (create and supersede), story_reporting.move_story_stage, repair_story_versions, content_item_lifecycle create/assignment, assignments_workflow Item upserts, copywriting, story_triggers, editor_review, story_selection, story_commands, seed_edition, markus_import. No extra write and no extra read per save. The authoring client checks once per process that the site's Item type has headStageKey (graphql_type_field_names) and drops the field when it does not, so a new CLI still works against a site not yet deployed. A test-only invariant (fake client) asserts after every backend scenario that each lineage has at most one row with headStageKey and that it equals that row's stage. Acceptance: Gherkin writer scenarios pass; invariant hook on; writes per save unchanged (asserted by the request meter).
